sections.title: Design header
sections.template:
| | |
|---|---|
| **System** | _One sentence: the agent system this design is about_ |
| **Decisions record (Level 3)** | _where your decisions live, if you have one_ |
| **Owner** | _the accountable person_ |
| **Status** | Draft v0.1 |
| **Date** | _today_ |

**Scope.** _What the agent may do, and what it is not allowed to do._

sections.title: 1. Workflows, assistants and agents: choosing the shape
sections.template:
## 1. Workflows, assistants and agents: choosing the shape

**Lab:** Describe the task and decide the shape

**Task 1.** Describe the task in three sentences: who asks, what the input is, what a good result looks like and who checks it.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** List the three shapes for your task and say, in a sentence each, how it would work.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** Score the four signals (path unknown, result checkable, wrong step cheap to undo, cost acceptable) as yes, partly or no, with a reason for each.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** Write the decision record: choice, reasons, rejected options and the event that would make you revisit it.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** The task description, the signal scores with reasons, and the five-line decision record.

sections.title: 2. The agentic loop and tools as contracts
sections.template:
## 2. The agentic loop and tools as contracts

**Lab:** Define the tools and their contracts

**Task 1.** List every tool your system needs, at least four, with a one-sentence purpose each.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** Write a contract for each tool: inputs with types and limits, outputs, side effects, errors and callers.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** Classify each tool as read only, reversible change or irreversible or external effect.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** For every changing tool, write the limit and the place in code where it is enforced.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** A table of tools with contract, class and enforced limit.

sections.title: 3. Levels of autonomy and the human in the loop
sections.template:
## 3. Levels of autonomy and the human in the loop

**Lab:** Set permissions, budgets and approval points

**Task 1.** Rate each tool low, medium or high criticality with a one-line reason, and give it an autonomy level from 0 to 3.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** Design the approval for every tool at level 1: what the approver sees, who may approve and when it expires.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** Set a budget for one run: maximum steps, maximum tool calls, maximum cost and maximum time, and say what happens at the limit.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** Define the handover note and list at least three stop conditions.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** The autonomy table, one approval design, the run budget and the handover note.

sections.title: 4. Context and memory as architecture
sections.template:
## 4. Context and memory as architecture

**Lab:** Design the memory and context

**Task 1.** For each step of your agent, list what it must know, where that comes from and how large it is.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** Choose working, session or long-term storage for each piece of information, with an owner and a retention period.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** Define trust labels for each source and where the label is stored so it survives a restart.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** Write the correction and deletion path for long-term memory, including who may use it and how fast.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** A context plan table, a memory table with owners and retention, the trust labels and the correction path.

sections.title: 5. Decisions as testable hypotheses
sections.template:
## 5. Decisions as testable hypotheses

**Lab:** Turn three decisions into testable hypotheses

**Task 1.** Name three high-risk decisions from your design so far, with a criticality tag and a reviewer.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** Write each as a hypothesis: the claim, the measurement and the number or result that would reverse it.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** Choose a cheap experiment for each and estimate its cost in hours.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** Record the first result or, if you have not run it, the date you will and the person who will.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** Three hypothesis records with experiments and reviewers.

sections.title: 6. Design exploration with AI: options, drivers and review points
sections.template:
## 6. Design exploration with AI: options, drivers and review points

**Lab:** Explore design options with AI and review them

**Task 1.** State the decision, your top three drivers with numbers and your hard constraints.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** Ask for three options of different kinds, each scored against every driver with its assumptions and failure points. Paste the useful parts.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** Check every score against your own numbers and list at least two things you corrected or rejected.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** Choose an option, name the reviewer and write the review points where a person must look.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** The decision, the prompt or request in summary, the options with your corrections, the choice and the review points.

sections.title: 7. Architecture knowledge agents can read: decision records, rules and specifications
sections.template:
## 7. Architecture knowledge agents can read: decision records, rules and specifications

**Lab:** Write the machine-readable architecture rules an agent must follow

**Task 1.** Write at least six rules as RULE-1 to RULE-6 or more, each with a statement and a reason, covering structure, tools, data and approval.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** Give every rule a VERIFIED_BY line naming the check, or a REVIEWED_BY line naming the role.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** Add an owner, a date and a status (active, superseded or proposed) to the rules file.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** Write the entry file of under 40 lines that points an agent to the rules, the decisions and the commands to build and test.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** The rules file with six or more rules, each with a check or a reviewer, and the entry file.

sections.title: 8. Delivering knowledge at the right moment: retrieval, skills and tool servers
sections.template:
## 8. Delivering knowledge at the right moment: retrieval, skills and tool servers

**Lab:** Design delivery of knowledge and test it

**Task 1.** List the knowledge your agent needs and assign each item to always loaded, retrieved or tool-provided, with a reason.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** Estimate the size of the always-loaded text and say what you cut to keep it small.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** Write at least ten test questions with the expected answer and the source that holds it.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** Run the questions (with a model or by hand), record the results and name the first fix you would make.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** The delivery table, the size estimate, the ten test questions and the results with a first fix.

sections.title: 9. A harness of preventive and detective controls
sections.template:
## 9. A harness of preventive and detective controls

**Lab:** Design the harness: a matrix of controls

**Task 1.** For every rule, name a preventive control and a detective control (or say why only one).

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** Describe each control in a word each for precision, coverage, speed and depth, and say where it runs.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** List at least five routine operations after which the controls must be retested, and say how.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** Write why each high-criticality control exists and the condition under which you would review or retire it.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** The control matrix, the operations list and the review conditions.

sections.title: 10. Architecture tests and drift checks in the pipeline
sections.template:
## 10. Architecture tests and drift checks in the pipeline

**Lab:** Write the tests that prove each rule, or mark it as a human review

**Task 1.** Write or describe a real check for at least three rules: the tool or test, the command to run it and the file where it lives.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** Say where each check runs and how long it takes, and mark any rule that only a person can review with the reviewer and the moment of review.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** If your code already breaks a rule, describe the baseline and the plan to shrink it, with a weekly number.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** For each check, describe the deliberate bad change that must make it fail and the result you saw or expect.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** Three checks with commands and locations, the baseline plan, and one must-fail example per check.

sections.title: 11. Extracting architecture from existing code, and checking what the agent found
sections.template:
## 11. Extracting architecture from existing code, and checking what the agent found

**Lab:** Extract an architecture view and verify what the agent found

**Task 1.** Name the slice, the commit or date and the artefacts you extracted from.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** List ten claims about building blocks, dependencies, interfaces or business rules, saying whether a tool or an agent produced each.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** Check each claim against evidence and mark it confirmed, wrong or unknown, with the evidence.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** Say what enters your documentation, what is rejected and when you will extract again.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** The slice, ten claims with evidence and verdicts, and the decision on what to publish.

sections.title: 12. Orchestration patterns and when multi-agent designs help
sections.template:
## 12. Orchestration patterns and when multi-agent designs help

**Lab:** Choose an orchestration pattern and contain failure between agents

**Task 1.** Choose the simplest pattern that fits your task and say why the simpler ones do not.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** If you propose more than one agent, justify each by a permission, context or skill; otherwise explain why one is enough.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** Define each hand-off as a schema with limits, a trust label and a check at the receiving side.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** Set a budget for each agent and for the whole system, and say where a run stops when a boundary is violated.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** The pattern choice, a one-page diagram or list of agents with tools and permissions, the hand-off schemas and the budgets.

sections.title: 13. Failure modes, retries and cost budgets
sections.template:
## 13. Failure modes, retries and cost budgets

**Lab:** Design failures, retries and cost budgets

**Task 1.** Write a failure table with at least six failure modes, each with detection, containment and recovery.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** For every changing tool, define the idempotency key, the retry limit and the waiting between tries.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** Define the checkpoints and describe the restart test you will run between two steps.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** Calculate the typical and worst-case cost and time per run with your own numbers, set the hard limits and say what happens when each is reached.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** The failure table, retry rules, checkpoints and the cost calculation with limits.

sections.title: 14. Evaluation plans and tracing
sections.template:
## 14. Evaluation plans and tracing

**Lab:** Write the evaluation and tracing plan

**Task 1.** Describe at least twenty cases across ordinary, hard, should-refuse and adversarial kinds, and where each comes from.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** Write numeric pass marks for success, safety, cost and time, and the number of runs per case, before any results.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** Choose a grader for each check, say how you will calibrate any model grader against a human, and name the limits.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** List the trace fields, the id that links them, what you redact and how long you keep traces.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** The case plan, the pass marks with numbers, the grader choices and the trace specification.

sections.title: 15. Governance, law and safe integrations
sections.template:
## 15. Governance, law and safe integrations

**Lab:** Write the governance and safe-integration record

**Task 1.** Make a data table: each data class, whether it may be sent to a model provider, and any redaction.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** Make a provider table with what each may see and an exit route you could actually follow.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** List each integration with its permission, how its secret is handled and its network or sandbox limit.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** Write the logging rule, the model-size rule and at least four legal questions with who will answer them and by when.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** The data table, provider table, integration list, logging rule and the dated legal questions.

sections.title: 16. Keeping judgment: ownership, skill and the architect’s changing role
sections.template:
## 16. Keeping judgment: ownership, skill and the architect’s changing role

**Lab:** Assign ownership and adoption, then write the architecture note an agent could read

**Task 1.** Make an ownership table: each important artefact with its named owner and reviewer.

_Your answer._

**Task 2.** Write your anti-atrophy rules: when a person must explain AI output, how much unaided practice, and your glossary of at least five domain terms.

_Your answer._

**Task 3.** Write an adoption hypothesis with two numeric metrics, a baseline, a target and a review date.

_Your answer._

**Task 4.** Write the architecture note an agent could read in under 40 lines: purpose, what the system may do, what it may never do, where the rules and checks live, the limits, and who to ask. Add the name of the person who signs it and the date.

_Your answer._

**Evidence to include:** The ownership table, the practice rules and glossary, the adoption hypothesis and the one-page note.
